thread:
maria: Anyone else seeing SCIM provisioning for acme-corp hitting 429s since last RBAC rollout? Started ~20m ago :warning:
kevin: I saw spikes. Edge: scim-provisioner returned 429 with Retry-After 30. No high QPS from client side though.
mar ia: Logs show a bunch of `permission denied` earlier from the service side then 429 flood. Suspect RBAC change toggled 'scim:write' to a new role? KMS key rotation happened ~an hour ago too.
jin: Can you paste the error blob? also check audit logs for the SCIM auth checks.
maria: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
x-scim-error: rate_limited
{"error":"rate_limited","inner":"permission_denied: key unseal failed"}
```
sam: Interesting inner says key unseal failed — likely KMS decrypt flakey. Did deploy-bot rotate keys?
deploy-bot: deploy: rotated kms-key alias redwood-scim-prod on 6219876000 by ops@infra — rotation completed, no error reported :gear:
kevin: If KMS unseal failed we sometimes return 500 not 429. Maybe flow: first requests hit a '403/permission_denied' due to RBAC, client retries aggressively, hits our global rate limiter and we return 429. Need to correlate initial 403s.
jin: Agree. Maria can you grep for `permission_denied` vs `kms` and the auth principal in the same trace id?
maria: Here's a typical trace (cut):
[scim] principal=svc-acme-scim role=svc-scim-v2 -> authz:deny reason='role_missing:scim.write'
then our retry loop issues 20 reqs, global token-bucket exhausted -> 429
TraceID: trc-0a9b
Full logs sent to #eng-logging
sam: Who rolled the RBAC change? I recall a canary where we renamed role 'scim.provision' -> 'scim.write' and backfilled some principals but not all. Could be a missing mapping for svc-acme-scim.
maria: @kevin @jin @sam ok I'm going to temporarily pin the acme tenant to legacy role mapping via feature flag to stop retries. Can someone check audit logs for role mappings and last-modified?
audit-bot: audit: role-change event by 'rbac-service' at 6219875900 {actor: infra-bot, change: rename scim.provision->scim.write, notes: staged rollout 100/100} (link: https://audit.internal/evt/6219875900)
kevin: Audit shows rename happened just before KMS rotate — that explains timing. We need two actions: 1) stop backoff/retries on client side and return 403 without retry, 2) reconcile missing principals or add temporary mapping.
jin: Also verify KMS alias was reparented. If key alias moved to a different CMK ID we might see transient decrypt errors when tokens are checked. Check kms logs for 'NotFoundException' or 'AccessDenied'.
sam: I ran a quick check: kms logs show a handful of AccessDenied for role=svc-acme-scim at 6219876050-6219876150. So both RBAC and KMS are implicated.
maria: Plan: 1) enable feature flag to map old role for svc-acme-scim (done) 2) roll back aggressive client retry policy to jittered exponential (will PR) 3) run backfill for principals missing new role 4) add audit alert for rename ops that also touch KMS — owner @kevin
kevin: :thumbsup: I'll own the backfill job and also add a post-rotate smoke test that does a SCIM write and validates decryption+authz. Rolling to ops-runbook now.
jin: For the immediate incident, can we clear token-bucket counters for acme-corp so they can resume? Otherwise they'll be stuck behind global limit even after fix.
sam: I cleared the quota bucket for tenant acme-corp (id=tn-acme-01). Monitor please.
maria: Thanks. Monitoring: error rate dropping, 429s -> an error every ~5m now. Leaving open to watch for 30m then we'll close. Will follow up with postmortem with timeline + mitigations.
kevin: Also add a check in rollout docs: when renaming RBAC roles tie the change to a mapping migration in identity store to avoid these gaps. Punting to RFC.
maria: :eyes: will draft the postmortem and link audit trace + KMS logs. Thanks all.
